body: I'm not sure if it was necessary to rename the context menu items instead of just renaming the setting keys. Before it was `script_editor/window_move_up` and now it's `script_editor/move_document_up` which is fine for the storage to distinguish them more easily. But it does bring a bit of confusion when you're working in different contexts like scripts, shaders, text files and so on. Now they're also do not display their shortcuts like they did in 4.7 because the defaults were removed. This can bring confusion for those who used the default shortcuts and now they won't work. 4.8: 4.7:

"Scripts" was never really correct in most of those cases (filter, navigate to) because the Script Editor can show documents that are not scripts like json files, other text files, and help documentation.
You are right that there is some inconsistency still, the "Reopen Closed Script" file menu item should be changed to use "Document" in the future, and same in the "Open Recent" submenu. But the other mentions of script "New Script" and "Soft Reload Tool Script" are correct because those are specifically about scripts and not other documents.

> I'm not sure if it was necessary to rename the context menu items instead of just renaming the setting keys. Before it was script_editor/window_move_up and now it's script_editor/move_document_up which is fine for the storage to distinguish them more easily. But it does bring a bit of confusion when you're working in different contexts like scripts, shaders, text files and so on.

The name in the context menu is the same as the name of the shortcut. It was changed because it was easy to mix up with another shortcut and it is not very clear in the shortcuts panel. And I don't see how clarifying what it moves is a problem, it applies to all documents.

> Now they're also do not display their shortcuts like they did in 4.7 because the defaults were removed. This can bring confusion for those who used the default shortcuts and now they won't work.

Because the shortcut was removed it makes sense that the shortcut is not shown. This seems like it would help users understand that there is no default shortcut for it now. I'm not sure how this would cause confusion.
The shortcut will show if one is assigned.

> Because the shortcut was removed it makes sense that the shortcut is not shown. This seems like it would help users understand that there is no default shortcut for it now.

That's exactly what I am talking about. Why the shortcut wasn't transferred to the new setting despite the setting being the same. 

Document just sounds strange to describe a script in the script editor (it's not called "Document editor" and the tab in Godot is called "Script" and not "Document") or a shader in the shader editor. But maybe it's just me. Because we are talking about the user interface in the engine and not about the internal structure that can be and is different.

See the proposal for context on why the defaults were removed:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/15233

>      That's exactly what I am talking about. Why the shortcut wasn't transferred to the new setting despite the setting being the same.

If there was a custom shortcut then it is transferred to the new shortcut. But the default shortcut can't really be transferred since removing the default shortcut was the point.

> Document just sounds strange to describe a script in the script editor (it's not called "Document editor" and the tab in Godot is called "Script" and not "Document") or a shader in the shader editor. But maybe it's just me. Because we are talking about the user interface in the engine and not about the internal structure that can be and is different.

Hopefully its just because its new and it won't sound strange in the future.
The main purpose of the Script Editor is still to edit Scripts, so I think its fine to keep the name as "Script Editor" and the tab as "Script", in addition to other reasons. But functionally, terms in actions that operate on other types than Scripts should be made more accurate to prevent confusion when someone expected it to only work on scripts.
It also helps with code deduplication to use "Document", so we can use the same shortcuts for both the Script Editor and Shader Editor. And so we don't have to change "Script" to "Shader" all over the place in the Shader Editor.
There are a few other shortcuts that need to be changed actually, "Next Script" and "Previous Script".

"Document" is the best word I could think of, there's reasons to not use "file" or other words here, and other IDEs use "document" similarly.
- related https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/28607#issuecomment-3765867783
